title: Git Model Of Self
definition: The concept of understanding the self as a version-controlled system, with each version representing a different configuration or deployment of the self.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of yourself as a software program. Different parts of your life are like different versions of the code. You can go back to a previous version, make changes, and merge insights from different versions.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: The Git Model of Self posits that the self is a dynamic, layered, and version-controlled system. Experiences, learnings, and modifications are like commits, while the coherence and continuity of the self are represented by the branch structure.
difficulty_levels.expert: The Git Model of Self extends the metaphor of version control to the human mind. It connects to the non-self doctrine of anattā, predictive processing, and trauma theory. It resolves the tension in trauma theory by recognizing that experiences change the self, yet the pre-trauma self persists as a deployment in the version history. The model also engages with the concept of 'self' in physics, where the self is seen as a complex system of interacting parts.

extra_fields.insight: The self is a git log.
